picks.editorial_note: A $39.5M ARPA-H consortium uniting Boston University with Philips, Johns Hopkins, and Weill Cornell signals serious federal and industry investment in AI-enabled robotic stroke intervention — the kind of cross-sector funding that can move a technology from lab to bedside.
picks.title: Brink Bites: Robotic Stroke Surgery, Curbing Junk Food Sales, and American Attitudes On Data Center Construction

picks.editorial_note: MIT's Regina Barzilay and Jim Collins winning the Pritzker Prize for AI-enabled antibiotic discovery is a marquee validation of AI's ability to drive genuine scientific breakthroughs in drug discovery.
picks.title: Regina Barzilay and Jim Collins win Pritzker Prize for AI and Science Research Excellence for work in AI-enabled antibiotic discovery

picks.editorial_note: Nebraska's role leading cybersecurity for the $24.5M national FabAID project, under the Morgridge Institute, shows how AI-driven science infrastructure is becoming a coordinated multi-institution national priority.
picks.title: University to lead cybersecurity for national Fabric for AI-Driven Science project

picks.editorial_note: HKUST and HSBC's strategic framework agreement, anchored by HSBC's new AI & Emerging Technology Institute, deepens a near-decade academia-finance alliance and shows how major banks are formalizing AI R&D partnerships with universities.
picks.title: HKUST and HSBC Forge Strategic Partnership to Advance AI, Emerging Technologies and Financial Innovation
picks.university: Hong Kong Univ. of Science and Technology

picks.editorial_note: Michigan State's $30M capital-backed TEMPEST turbulence research center shows state-level commitment to building physical infrastructure that fuses physics, computation, and AI.
picks.title: MSU trustees receive presentation on new turbulence research center, approve state capital outlay request

picks.editorial_note: Anthropic's pledge of up to $100 billion in equity to the public, alongside SpaceX's giveaways, raises major questions about how AI windfalls should be distributed — a financial story with outsized policy implications for the field.
picks.title: Billions in SpaceX, Anthropic Stock Pledged to the Public. Who Benefits? - Georgetown University

picks.editorial_note: Tel Aviv University and Stanford researchers showing AI models can learn general predictive skills from purely synthetic self-generated data challenges assumptions about the necessity of real-world training data.
picks.title: AI Learns to Predict the World Without Ever Seeing It

picks.editorial_note: HKUST's HK$100 million RAISe+ commercialization fund, paired with its EmArm robotic research, reflects substantial institutional investment in translating AI research into deployable technology.
picks.title: October Research & Innovation Roundup
picks.university: Hong Kong Univ. of Science and Technology

picks.editorial_note: A $3.2M NIH-funded ASU project using deep learning on retinal images and blood biomarkers to screen for preclinical Alzheimer's could enable earlier, less invasive detection of the disease.
picks.title: What the eye may reveal about Alzheimer’s

picks.editorial_note: Inria's symposium at the French National Assembly on combating AI-driven disinformation puts AI misuse directly in front of national policymakers, underscoring growing government attention to AI governance.
picks.title: Inria Symposium – Combating the Manipulation of Information: Immediate Solutions and Challenges Ahead
